artifacts.title: Jennings v. North Florida Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: North Florida Presbytery was found to have erred in restoring deposed minister A. B. Scott to the office of Teaching Elder by a vote of 19-17, which the SJC determined did not satisfy the BCO 34-8 requirement that 'the general sentiment of the Church is strongly in his favor.' The SJC annulled NFP's actions and remanded the case; a lengthy dissent by RE Donahoe argued that BCO 34-8 does not require a super-majority and that the restoration vote is distinct from the evaluation of general sentiment.

artifacts.synopsis: Northern California Presbytery adopted an abstract resolution declaring six different views on the diaconate permissible for ministers and Sessions; the SJC sustained the complaints and annulled the resolution, holding that no court may issue binding abstract decrees beyond its proper jurisdictional exercise. A concurring opinion analyzed each of the six diaconal views in detail and set out standards (the GUMP/Kniseley framework) for when diaconal assistant practices are constitutionally permissible.

artifacts.synopsis: Complainant alleged that Pacific Presbytery erred in not opposing the ordination of Lee Irons as a Ruling Elder at New Life Burbank, given that Pacific Presbytery had previously denied Irons's application as a Teaching Elder candidate; the SJC denied the complaint, holding that each court retains discretion to evaluate candidates for ordination within its jurisdiction and that Presbytery's denial for Teaching Elder did not preclude a Session's ordination of the same man as Ruling Elder.

artifacts.title: Sartorious et al. v. Siouxlands Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC denied a complaint that Siouxlands Presbytery erred in finding no strong presumption of guilt in TE Joshua Moon after an investigation into allegations that his theological views on Federal Vision topics were heterodox, holding that deference to the presbytery was required absent clear error in the record. The case generated a concurring opinion offering procedural guidance on BCO 31-2 investigations versus BCO 32-2 charges, and a dissenting opinion by RE Haigler arguing the record showed unambiguous heterodoxy warranting a finding of strong presumption of guilt.

artifacts.title: Carpenter v. Siouxlands
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC found that Presbytery of Siouxlands erred in denying a complaint that sought the appointment of a committee to conduct a BCO 31-2 investigation into whether TE Greg Lawrence held or taught views associated with Federal Vision theology contrary to the PCA's doctrinal standards. The Court directed that the presbytery conduct the required investigation and established that credible reports affecting Christian character warrant investigation regardless of the evidentiary standards required for conviction.

artifacts.synopsis: Complaint of TE Morton H. Smith vs. Western Carolina Presbytery. The SJC sustained Smith's complaint in part, finding that Presbytery erred procedurally by immediately adopting a judgment against RE Payne's views without process. The SJC annulled the declaration made by Presbytery regarding RE Payne's views and remanded the case for proper adjudication.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Martin Payne and related complainants challenged Western Carolina Presbytery's BCO 31-2 investigation of accusations concerning TE Craig Bulkeley and its conclusion that no strong presumption of guilt existed. The SJC denied the specifications, holding that BCO 31-2 gives the investigating court great discretion over procedure and timing and that the record did not show clear error; related complainants lacked standing.

artifacts.synopsis: Rocky Mountain Presbytery sustained a candidate's ordination exam who held the view that women could teach (but not preach or exercise authority) in church ministries under the authority of the church session. TE James Urish complained that Presbytery erred in sustaining the candidate's exam. The SJC affirmed Presbytery's decision, finding no clear error, as neither the Westminster Standards nor the BCO explicitly address this specific application of 1 Timothy 2:12.

artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Crossroads Community Church challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's licensing and ordination of a candidate who stated a difference concerning women and the office of deacon but agreed to follow the BCO. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed presbytery's judgment, holding that the candidate's stated willingness to comply with the BCO and affirm the ordination vow supported the decision; a dissent argued the complaint should have been sustained.

artifacts.title: Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Michael Chastain appealed his conviction and indefinite suspension by Heritage Presbytery for divisive behavior, arising from his public letters to his congregation disagreeing with Session actions regarding an associate pastor call and a related Christian school controversy. The SJC denied the appeal (20-1), upholding the conviction and censure while finding procedural errors that did not rise to reversible level; a dissent by RE Frederick Neikirk argued the charge of 'divisive behavior' failed BCO 29-1's requirement that offenses be proven from Scripture.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Peter B. Kim appealed his deposition and excommunication by Korean Eastern Presbytery on charges of contumacy and threatening members with civil litigation. The SJC sustained the contumacy charge and deposition but reduced the excommunication to indefinite suspension from the sacraments as excessive; it declined to rule on the civil-threat charge because the relevant letter was not in the Record of the Case.
